_comment: The complete interface between the harness and whatever launches it. This file is the
ONLY thing the two sides share; they share no code at all.
That is deliberate. A shared Python package does not even guarantee agreement — a pip
install served a stale engine out of a Docker layer cache exactly once, which is how
the lesson was learned — whereas a versioned contract can be tested independently from
both sides. The harness asserts it honours this file; the loader asserts every spec it
It is also served live at GET /v1/contract, so a loader can validate against the
contract of the exact image it is about to launch rather than against a vendored copy

env._comment: Supplied BY the loader, consumed BY the harness. The harness computes none of these; it refuses to start rather than defaulting, because every default is a second definition of something the loader owns.

required_always.PODH_WORKSPACE: root of the mounted data view, e.g. /workspace
required_always.PODH_LOG_ROOT: directory for run output. The harness used to derive this as $PODH_WORKSPACE/runs, which meant the layout was defined here AND in the loader; the copies drifted three times in one day.

required_for_batch.PODH_JOB_ID: the job this pod owns. Assigned at creation, never discovered — workers that scan for work can race, and object storage cannot arbitrate.
required_for_batch.PODH_JOB_SPEC: absolute path to the job spec, written BEFORE the pod is created
required_for_batch.PODH_RUN_PREFIX: object-key prefix where this job publishes status, e.g. runs/<job_id>
required_for_batch.PODH_WRITE_PREFIXES: comma-separated object-key prefixes this job may write to. The harness refuses any write outside them. A harness that could write anywhere could overwrite corpus/raw/, the one thing here that cannot be regenerated.

optional.PODH_CODE_ROOT: path to the workload's code; prepended to PYTHONPATH. Absent means run the image's baked code, and the harness says which it used.
optional.PODH_API_TOKEN: bearer token for /v1. Absent disables the API.
optional.PODH_ENTRY: override the batch entry module (default pod_harness.execute_job)
optional.MAX_LIFE_SEC: in-pod deadline. DETECTS but cannot terminate — runpodctl inside a pod returns Unauthorized, so cost control must be external.

provider_supplied.RUNPOD_POD_ID: set by RunPod; used only for labelling, never for logic

spec._comment: Written by the loader, read by the harness. `params` is opaque to both — only the workload interprets it. Everything else is framework surface the harness acts on.

idempotency_key.description: optional, unique. A re-POST returns the existing job rather than starting a second pod-hour — agents retry on timeout, and this makes that safe.

root.description: immutable code/<workload>/<rev>/, or code/<workload>/dev/ for iteration

stages_from.description: module:attribute naming the workload's stage registry

runner.description: how to provision. The harness ignores this entirely — it is the loader talking to itself, carried in the spec so a job record is self-describing.

from.description: auto | <stage name> | never. `auto` re-runs verify_outputs() per completed stage and restarts at the first that does not verify. Never marker-driven: a .DONE marker once survived a wiped volume and reported 'done: 24' over no outputs.

events._comment: Written by the harness, read by the loader. Append-only JSON lines plus an atomically-replaced status.json snapshot.

files.$PODH_RUN_PREFIX/status.json: the same snapshot in object storage, so status survives the pod

seq.description: monotonic per job. A client resumes from where it stopped on any transport.

invariants: `state` carries StageResult.status verbatim. Collapsing `unverified` into `ok` would make status report green for exactly the bug class the verification layer exists to catch: three separate bugs where a stage reported success and produced nothing.
`seq` never decreases and never repeats within a job.
A terminal job answers a long-poll immediately rather than waiting out the timeout.

api._comment: Identical on a pod and on a control plane, so a client written against one works against the other. That is what lets compute move to serverless or another vendor without touching callers.
api.auth: Bearer token or X-Podh-Token header; /v1/health is unauthenticated

endpoints.note: discovery: endpoints, stage vocabulary, spec schema
this file, as served by the running harness

invariants: No unbounded responses: every payload is capped and reports total_bytes/truncated.
dry_run costs nothing and starts no stage.
Submit is idempotent when idempotency_key is supplied.
Errors carry a `hint` naming the fix.

responses._comment: Response shapes a loader depends on. Added because my own polling scripts read `state` twice in one day when the job endpoint returns `job_state` — the poll silently reported None while the job had genuinely failed. An endpoint list is not enough; the keys are part of the interface.

properties.job_state: queued | running | done | failed | cancelled — NOT `state`
properties.seq: integer, cursor into the event stream
properties.stages: object keyed by stage name; each has state, index, seconds, verification
